reconstructed_theorem_text: For every natural number n >= 3 and every real kappa >= 4, let mu be normalized Haar probability measure on the full real orthogonal group O(n), equipped with its Borel sigma-algebra. Let h: R -> R be Borel measurable and assume integral_{O(n)} |h(O_{00})| dmu(O) < infinity. Define A_kappa(O) = ((kappa+1)/2) I_n - ((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T), and let all square roots denote nonnegative real square roots. Then integral_{O(n)} det(O) sqrt(det(A_kappa(O))) h(O_{00}) dmu(O) = [(-1)^(n-1) (sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1) / 2^n] integral_{O(n)} [ (sqrt(kappa)+1) O_{00} - (sqrt(kappa)-1) ] h(O_{00}) dmu(O).
objects: The dimension n; the real parameter kappa; the full orthogonal group O(n); its normalized Haar probability measure mu; a Borel measurable real function h; the real matrix A_kappa(O) = ((kappa+1)/2) I_n - ((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T); the determinant of O; the nonnegative square root of det(A_kappa(O)); and two real-valued group integrals.
domains: n ranges over natural numbers with n >= 3, and kappa ranges over real numbers with kappa >= 4. h maps R to R. O ranges over all real n by n orthogonal matrices, with both determinant signs and with the inherited matrix topology and Borel sigma-algebra. O_{00} is the zero-based first diagonal entry. Every integral is with respect to normalized Haar probability measure mu on the entire group O(n).
quantifiers: For every natural n >= 3, every real kappa >= 4, and every Borel measurable h: R -> R such that integral |h(O_{00})| dmu(O) < infinity, the displayed integral identity holds.
assumptions: n >= 3; kappa >= 4; h is Borel measurable; and O -> h(O_{00}) is absolutely Bochner L1 integrable under normalized Haar measure mu on the full orthogonal group. The integrability assumption concerns this composition, without imposing global boundedness or real-line L1 integrability on h.
conclusion: With A_kappa(O) = ((kappa+1)/2) I_n - ((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T), integral det(O) sqrt(det(A_kappa(O))) h(O_{00}) dmu(O) equals (-1)^(n-1) (sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1) / 2^n times integral [ (sqrt(kappa)+1) O_{00} - (sqrt(kappa)-1) ] h(O_{00}) dmu(O). The statement asserts this equality and does not separately assert integrability of the two displayed weighted integrands.
scopes: n, kappa and h are fixed across the identity. Each integral binds its own orthogonal matrix O, and every occurrence of O within one integrand denotes that same matrix. The square root in the first integrand is applied to the scalar determinant of A_kappa(O). The factor (-1)^(n-1) (sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1) / 2^n multiplies the entire second integral. All square roots are nonnegative real square roots, powers have natural-number exponents, and n-1 is natural-number subtraction. Both integrals use the same normalized Haar law on the full O(n).
constant_dependencies: There are no existential or unspecified constants. The dimension threshold is the fixed number 3 and the parameter threshold is the fixed number 4. The matrix coefficients are exactly (kappa+1)/2 and (kappa-1)/4. The prefactor is exactly (-1)^(n-1) (sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1) / 2^n and depends only on n and kappa. The scalar coefficients in the second integrand are sqrt(kappa)+1 and sqrt(kappa)-1. The probability measure depends only on n.
